_readme: Filled 2026-09-07 from the phone, then corrected twice against Peter's account. Read the
distance note before changing any number here.
DISTANCE = 50.36, AND IT COMES FROM STRAVA, NOT THIS RIG.
Late in the day Peter put the Apple Watch on to charge and it stopped recording distance.
Strava kept running, so he trusted Strava and manually pushed the live site forward to
match -- twice, an hour or two apart. /var/root/race/dist_override holds 50.36, written
17:47 on race day, and state.json's dist_src was 'override' as a result.
So the phone's own distance series is NOT an independent measurement after the watch
dropped out. Corroborating evidence that it is unusable end-to-end: dist.csv shows the
counter COLLAPSING TO ZERO twice and being re-read from scratch (a +23.10 step to 23.10 at
6h36m, and a +49.70 step to 49.70 at 16h34m).
Three figures that are WRONG and must not be reinstated:
- 50.596 (phone_reported_mi): the override plus later walking around the party.
- 70,122 s: just the clock when the stack was stopped at 21:33.
- 17h 12m: the first dist.csv row past 50.00. Meaningless -- the series had already
collapsed and been manually pushed by then.
Milestone splits were removed for the same reason: two collapse-to-zero events mean the
10/20/30/40-mile times cannot be trusted.
START 02:34:37, FINISH 17:11:25 -> 14h 36m 48s. Both exact, from Peter.
The 02:05:09 in start_epoch is when `race reset` was run, ~29 min before he actually set
off; telemetry_start keeps it only to explain the gap. Do not compute elapsed from it.
This is the FOURTH correction to the timing, all four from Peter rather than the data: the
stack's stop time, a phantom 50.00 crossing, reset-vs-start-line, then these exact times.
The lesson is structural -- the rig records when commands were typed and when counters
moved, and neither is when a person started or stopped running. Every time on the page
rests on Peter's account by design.
Pace is derived from 14h 36m 48s and 50.36.
SOLID, because it never touched the watch or the override:
hr_avg 116, hr_max 140   Polar H10 chest strap, restricted to 02:34:37-17:11:25.
Read this before 'fixing' the peak back up. The earlier hr_max of 199 was an ARTIFACT,
twice over:
1. The 199.5 occurred at 17:21:51 -- TEN MINUTES AFTER Peter finished, almost certainly
him taking the strap off. Excluding post-finish data removes it outright.
2. It was derived as 60000/rr_ms, and the rr column contains split beats. The highest
in-window rr value gives 174.5 bpm at 03:25:19 from rr=343.8 ms -- immediately
followed by rr=715.8 ms. Those sum to 1059 ms, i.e. two normal ~535 ms beats, so one
beat was double-counted. The strap's own hr_bpm read 111 straight through it.
So HR now comes from the strap's OWN hr_bpm column, not from rr_ms. Inside the window that
column never exceeds 140 and has ZERO samples above 170. Highest sustained 30 s: 138.7.
The average barely moved (115.5 either way) -- with 100,252 samples one bad beat cannot
shift a mean. Only the peak was ever fragile.
trail_out_and_back_mi  22, the Los Gatos Creek Trail out-and-back with Leo from 02:30.
people_*          Peter's estimates, ~125 over the day and ~30 on the last lap. Rendered
with a leading ~. They replace the opt-in tracker's 11 sign-ins and 6
movers, which were real but wildly unrepresentative.
SOFT:
steps, kcal       phone pedometer, unaffected by the watch but INCLUDING the hours of
walking around the Oktoberfest afterwards. Fine as colour, not a claim.
climb_ft          NOT AVAILABLE anywhere: trail.txt is epoch/lat/lon only and no HealthKit
workout was ever written.
route map         NOT POSSIBLE from the phone: TRAIL_KEEP=3000 had trimmed trail.txt to the
last 3000 fixes, spanning 21 m x 39 m. Export the GPX from Strava.
